sources.title: Verification of Autonomous Systems
sources.publisher: NASA Langley Research Center / NASA Technical Reports Server
sources.inspection_scope: Retained and inspected the NASA milestone presentation, including physical PDF slide/page 12 for the stated Simplex overview. It remains a research presentation, not certification guidance.

regions.locator: PDF physical slide/page 12, Basic structure of a simplex architecture
regions.excerpt: If the monitor is triggered, a trusted component takes over operation.

sources.limitations: Search-index excerpt only; no full presentation context or proof details. Treat as NASA research communication, not certification guidance.

sources.title: A Formal Verification Framework for Runtime Assurance
sources.publisher: NASA Langley Research Center / NASA Technical Reports Server
sources.inspection_scope: Inspected NASA NTRS indexed abstract and metadata for the 2024 NASA Formal Methods Symposium presentation; downloadable PDF was not opened.

regions.excerpt: Instantiations may be kept at varying levels of generality, allowing for black box components.

sources.limitations: Abstract-level inspection. Demonstration is a proof of concept using an automatic vehicle braking system; it does not establish deployability or certification acceptance.

sources.title: A Verification Framework for Runtime Assurance of Autonomous UAS
sources.publisher: NASA Langley Research Center / NASA Technical Reports Server
sources.inspection_scope: Inspected NASA NTRS indexed abstract and search-indexed paper text for the Simplex assumptions, PVS/Plaidypvs formalization, black-box modeling and monitor sampling-rate consequence; NTRS page itself returned 403 on open.

regions.excerpt: Assuming that the sample rate of the monitor will detect improper functioning with enough time
formal verification of a system with an untrusted black box component

sources.limitations: Research formalization does not address many industrial deployment difficulties. A verified abstract model does not prove sensor timing, plant model fidelity or implementation correctness.

sources.title: Multi-Platform, Multi-Architecture Runtime Verification of Autonomous Space Systems
sources.jurisdiction: US research; autonomous space systems and UAS
sources.inspection_scope: Inspected NASA project page describing R2U2 runtime verification and system health management, including monitored components and responsiveness/realizability/unobtrusiveness goals.

regions.excerpt: continuously monitor essential system components such as sensors, software, and hardware
Responsiveness means evaluating system health in real time, with provable timing and performance guarantees.

sources.limitations: Project description, not a completed assurance case or operational approval. Claims about provable timing describe the intended property of the framework.

sources.title: Roadmap for Artificial Intelligence Safety Assurance, Version I
sources.inspection_scope: Inspected FAA landing page and the 31-page Version I PDF, including executive summary, guiding principles, learned-versus-learning distinction and responsibility/change passages on pages 3, 7-11.

regions.excerpt: Differentiate between Learned and Learning AI
Learned AI Implementation: AI implementations that are static in the operating environment.
Learning AI implementations may adapt in a manner that degrades performance

sources.limitations: A roadmap gives principles and plans, not a type certificate, means of compliance or approval for a specific model. Current FAA policy and later versions require refresh.

sources.title: Artificial Intelligence Concept Paper Issue 2: Guidance for Level 1 & 2 machine-learning applications
sources.inspection_scope: Inspected EASA publication page and its stated scope for Level 1/2, learning assurance, explainability and human-AI teaming; full PDF not extracted.

regions.excerpt: deepens the exploration of 'learning assurance', 'AI explainability' and 'ethics-based assessment'
AI systems that automatically take decisions under human oversight

sources.limitations: EASA concept paper is guidance and research input, not itself an approval. Page-level summary is insufficient for detailed means-of-compliance claims; Proposed Issue 03 appeared in 2026 and must be treated separately.

sources.title: IPC Project ForMuLA — Formal Methods Use for Learning Assurance
sources.publisher: European Union Aviation Safety Agency and Collins Aerospace
sources.inspection_scope: Inspected EASA report page for applicability, formal-methods objectives, demonstrated estimator use and stated scalability challenge; public PDF was not extracted.

regions.excerpt: Formal methods can be applied to assess machine-learning model stability, robustness, and compliance
Scalability and applicability of formal methods tools need further development

sources.limitations: The page says the report does not recommend specific methods or tools and frames the work as theoretical opportunities plus one industrial estimator demonstration. It does not prove an airborne control application.

sources.title: Concepts of Design Assurance for Neural Networks (CoDANN)
sources.publisher: European Union Aviation Safety Agency and Daedalean
sources.inspection_scope: Inspected EASA publication summary for W-shaped learning assurance, generalization, safety assessment and data/robustness challenges; PDF was not extracted.

regions.excerpt: The report introduces a W-shaped development cycle for 'learning assurance'
Addressing data completeness and representativeness, bias/variance trade-off, and robustness

sources.limitations: Publication summary only. It describes concepts and a visual-landing use case, not a certification decision or evidence that a deployed aircraft system meets the concepts.

sources.title: ISO/PAS 8800:2024 — Road vehicles — Safety and artificial intelligence
sources.inspection_scope: Inspected ISO public standard page and abstract, including covered AI-related vehicle risks, external AI interactions, out-of-scope external-element development and publication status.

regions.excerpt: This document addresses the risk of undesired safety-related behaviour at the vehicle level
The development of AI elements that are not part of the vehicle is not within the scope

sources.limitations: Only ISO's public abstract was inspected; the 172-page licensed text and conformity procedures were not. Publication status does not show product adoption or compliance.

sources.title: ISO 21448:2022 — Road vehicles — Safety of the intended functionality
sources.inspection_scope: Inspected ISO public abstract for SOTIF definition, complex-sensor situational awareness, operation-phase measures and scope exclusions.

regions.excerpt: absence of unreasonable risk due to a hazard caused by functional insufficiencies
proper situational awareness is essential to safety

sources.limitations: Public abstract only; not a substitute for the licensed standard. SOTIF scope is road-vehicle-specific and cannot be transferred to aviation certification by analogy.

sources.title: UL 4600 Edition 3 Updates Incorporate Autonomous Trucking
sources.jurisdiction: Autonomous products; road and off-road examples
sources.inspection_scope: Inspected UL Solutions overview of Edition 3, technology-agnostic scope, safety-case evidence expectations and multiple-framework relationship.

regions.excerpt: a goal-based and technology-agnostic Standard covering autonomous vehicles
analysis, simulation, closed course testing and safe public road testing

sources.limitations: UL's explanation is not the complete standard and is from a standards service provider. It describes safety-case expectations, not a universal pass threshold or government operating authorization.

sources.title: VeriSig: verifying safety properties of hybrid systems with neural network controllers
sources.inspection_scope: Inspected ACM Digital Library abstract and bibliographic record for neural-network/plant composition, sigmoid restriction, reachability and case studies.

regions.excerpt: transform the problem into a hybrid system verification problem
We focus on sigmoid-based networks

sources.limitations: The method's claims depend on specified activation functions and plant models; two case studies do not establish broad scalability or operational assurance.

sources.title: Interval Reachability of Nonlinear Dynamical Systems with Neural Network Controllers
sources.inspection_scope: Inspected PMLR paper page, abstract, method summary and case-study statement for inclusion functions, mixed-monotone embedding and hyper-rectangular reachable-set over-approximation.

regions.excerpt: rigorous verification of nonlinear continuous-time dynamical systems with neural network controllers
compute hyper-rectangular over-approximations of the reachable sets

sources.limitations: Results are model-based and use tunable partitioning/over-approximation. Abstract does not establish perception robustness, sensor independence or flight certification.

sources.title: Risk verification of stochastic systems with neural network controllers
sources.jurisdiction: Research method; autonomous car and underwater vehicle cases
sources.inspection_scope: Inspected ScienceDirect abstract for data-driven trace-robustness risk, nominal-to-perturbed risk gap and F1/10 car/underwater vehicle case studies.

regions.excerpt: a data-driven framework for verifying the risk of stochastic dynamical systems
the tightness of this bound depends on the closeness of the systems

sources.limitations: Data-driven risk estimates depend on trajectory data, specification robustness and assumptions such as Lipschitz continuity or incremental stability; estimated risk is not a universal probability of safety.

sources.title: Discovering governing equations from data by sparse identification of nonlinear dynamical systems
sources.publisher: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
sources.inspection_scope: Inspected PNAS indexed abstract text for SINDy sparse-regression formulation, governing-equation examples and stated dependence on measurement variables, data quality and library basis.

regions.excerpt: most physical systems have only a few relevant terms
depends on the choice of measurement variables, data quality, and the sparsifying function basis

sources.limitations: SINDy identifies candidate dynamics under structural, measurement and data assumptions. Its compactness does not make a learned perception or control model safe by itself.

sources.title: Don't trust your eyes: on the (un)reliability of feature visualizations
sources.inspection_scope: Inspected Google DeepMind publication page and abstract for adversarial visualization circuits, natural-input mismatch and theoretical limitation for black-box networks.

regions.excerpt: feature visualizations are processed very differently from standard input
does not include black-box neural networks

sources.limitations: The paper studies feature visualization, not all interpretability methods. A limitation of visualization cannot be generalized to every causal or mechanistic analysis.

sources.title: Mapping the mind of a large language model
sources.inspection_scope: Inspected Anthropic research page for stated feature coverage, computational cost, representation-versus-circuit distinction and unresolved safety-use question.

regions.excerpt: The features we found represent a small subset of all the concepts learned
Understanding the representations the model uses doesn't tell us how it uses them

sources.limitations: Language-model interpretability evidence is not evidence about vehicle perception/control models. Anthropic's page is a laboratory report, not an independent safety evaluation.
